full_judgment: 7. Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents submits that the defendant respondent bank published the auction notice under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in the newspaper on 20.5.2005 fixing 04.06.2005 as the date for holding auction giving 15(fifteen) days time out of which 4 days were government holidays. But section 48 of the said Ain provides that for the purpose of limitation only the working days are to be counted and as such, the bank violated the law in publishing the auction notice which the trial court failed to consider and most erroneously held that the bank followed the provisions of law in publishing the auction notice. The High Court Division on the other hand rightly decided the issue and decreed the suit. Thus, the impugned Judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division does not call for interference. He next submits that defendant No.3 in collusion with defendant No. 1, bank managed to submit 04(four) quotations showing one of them to be the highest bidder who purchased the mortgaged property at a shockingly low price keeping the plaintiffs in dark. Referring to the evidence of DW.2, former Manager of the bank, learned Advocate for the respondent submits that DW.2 in his cross Examination, admitted that the auction notice was published only giving only 12 days time which is completely violative of the provisions of the said Ain. Referring to the decisions in the case of Abdul Jalil Vs. Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and another reported in 41 DLR(AD)109 and in the case of Md. Moklesur Rahman and another Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 23 BLT(AD)210, the learned Advocate for the respondent prays for dis-missing the civil petition.
